records.source: אִם־תָּשׁ֨וּב יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל׀נְאֻם־יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י תָּשׁ֑וּב וְאִם־תָּסִ֧יר שִׁקּוּצֶ֛יךָ מִפָּנַ֖י וְלֹ֥א תָנֽוּד׃
records.gloss: If you return, Israel, declares Yahweh, to me you will return; and if you remove your detestable things from before me, and not you will wander,
pieces: If you return, Israel, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. If you put your detestable idols out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight and no longer stray,

L.1: If you return, Israel, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} you shall return; and if you put away your detestable things from before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and do not wander,

R.1: Israel, if you come back, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. If you take your disgusting idols away from where I can see them and stop wandering away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}},

decisions.choice: if you return, return to me: Israel's turning must be a turning to the LORD himself
alternatives: if you return, Israel, you may come back (to your place, to favor)
decisions.reason: The verb "return" comes twice, and "to me" stands first in the second clause for emphasis. The call answers 3:10, where Judah turned back only "with falsehood": a real return is a return to the LORD himself. The second clause could also be read as a promise, "you may come back", restored to God's favor and the land (15:19 plays on the same verb in this way). Either way the condition is a return to God.

decisions.choice: detestable things: idols and the objects of foreign worship
decisions.reason: The word is used for idols and the gods they stand for, things the LORD finds loathsome (7:30; 13:27; 2 Kings 23:13, 24). Putting them away "from before me" means removing them from the LORD's presence, out of the land and the temple.

decisions.choice: wander: drift back and forth, stray
decisions.reason: The verb describes moving about with no settled place, as Cain was to be a wanderer (Genesis 4:12, 14). Here it pictures Israel drifting between the LORD and other gods (2:23, 36).

decisions.choice: the conditions run on into verse 2, where the result follows
decisions.reason: "If" governs several clauses (return, remove, do not wander, swear truly), and the promise for the nations comes only at the end of verse 2. The sentence continues across the verse division.

decisions.choice: detestable idols / disgusting idols ... wandering away from me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "idols" to show what the detestable things were (m2). Readable also says whom Israel wanders from, which the Hebrew leaves implied.

records.heading: If you return, Israel

records.source: וְנִשְׁבַּ֨עְתָּ֙ חַי־יְהוָ֔ה בֶּאֱמֶ֖ת בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט וּבִצְדָקָ֑ה וְהִתְבָּ֥רְכוּ ב֛וֹ גּוֹיִ֖ם וּב֥וֹ יִתְהַלָּֽלוּ׃ס
records.gloss: and you swear, [As] lives Yahweh, in truth, in justice and in righteousness, then will bless themselves in him nations, and in him they will boast.
pieces: and swear, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," \q in truth, with justice and with righteousness, \q then the nations will bless themselves by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and take pride in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.2: and swear, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," \q in truth, in justice and in righteousness, \q then nations will bless themselves by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} they will make their boast.

R.2: and if you make your promises by saying, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," \q and you mean it, and do what is fair and right, \q then the nations will ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to bless them, and they will be proud to belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: "As the LORD lives": the oath that calls on the living God as witness
decisions.reason: Israel was to swear by the LORD's name and by no other god (Deuteronomy 6:13; 10:20; Jeremiah 12:16). The oath counts only when it is backed by truth, justice and righteousness; in 5:2 the people say "As the LORD lives" and swear falsely.

decisions.choice: nations will bless themselves in him: the promise to Abraham fulfilled through Israel's return
decisions.reason: The same form of the verb is used in the promise to Abraham that all nations will bless themselves by his offspring (Genesis 22:18; 26:4; compare 12:3). When Israel turns back to God with a true heart, the nations will see it and seek blessing from Israel's God. The reflexive form can mean that they will invoke his name when they bless, or that they will find blessing for themselves in him.

decisions.choice: in him: the LORD
decisions.reason: The nearest person named is the LORD, by whom Israel swears, and boasting "in the LORD" is a common phrase (9:23; Psalm 34:3). The pronoun could point to Israel, as the one through whom blessing comes in Genesis, but the oath and the boasting both look to God.

decisions.choice: you mean it, and do what is fair and right ... proud to belong to him
decisions.reason: Readable puts the three nouns "in truth, in justice and in righteousness" as what the person swearing does, and spells out "boast in him" as being proud to belong to him.

decisions.choice: [As] the LORD lives (Literal); As surely as the LORD lives (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew oath is literally "living is the LORD". Literal brackets the supplied "As"; Balanced and Readable use the oath wording of 12:16 and of 1 Samuel.

records.source: כִּי־כֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֗ה לְאִ֤ישׁ יְהוּדָה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם נִ֥ירוּ לָכֶ֖ם נִ֑יר וְאַֽל־תִּזְרְע֖וּ אֶל־קוֹצִֽים׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh to [the] man of Judah and to Jerusalem: Break up for yourselves fallow ground, and do not sow among thorns.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this to the {{gender:people|men}} of Judah and to Jerusalem: \q Plow up your unplowed ground, \q and do not sow among thorns.

L.3: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the man of Judah and to Jerusalem: \q Break up for yourselves fallow ground, \q and do not sow among thorns.

R.3: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says to the people of Judah and Jerusalem: \q Your lives are like hard ground that needs plowing. Plow it up! \q Do not plant your seed among thorns.

decisions.choice: break up fallow ground: make a new start, as a farmer plows hard, neglected land before sowing
decisions.reason: Fallow ground has been left unplowed and has grown hard and weedy. Breaking it up is the first work before a new crop. Hosea uses the same words for seeking the LORD (Hosea 10:12): the people's lives must be turned over completely before anything good can grow.

decisions.choice: do not sow among thorns: do not add a show of repentance to lives still full of old sins
decisions.reason: Seed sown where thorns still grow is choked and comes to nothing (12:13; Genesis 3:18). A turning to God that leaves the old ways in place will not bear fruit.

decisions.choice: the man of Judah: everyone in Judah
decisions.reason: "Man" is singular here and stands for the whole population, men and women alike, as "inhabitant of Jerusalem" does (verse 4; Isaiah 5:3).

decisions.choice: the people of Judah
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the singular "man of Judah". Balanced and Readable say "people", since everyone in Judah is meant (m3).

decisions.choice: Your lives are like hard ground that needs plowing
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of plowing stands for, so that the reader does not take it as farming advice (m1).

records.heading: Plow up your unplowed ground

records.source: הִמֹּ֣לוּ לַיהֹוָ֗ה וְהָסִ֨רוּ֙ עָרְל֣וֹת לְבַבְכֶ֔ם אִ֥ישׁ יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם פֶּן־תֵּצֵ֨א כָאֵ֜שׁ חֲמָתִ֗י וּבָעֲרָה֙ וְאֵ֣ין מְכַבֶּ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י רֹ֥עַ מַעַלְלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Circumcise yourselves to Yahweh, and remove [the] foreskins of your heart, man of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, lest go out like fire my wrath and burn, and there is no one quenching, because of [the] evil of your deeds.
pieces: Circumcise yourselves for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; circumcise your hearts, \q {{gender:people|men}} of Judah and people of Jerusalem, \q or {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will flare up like fire and burn, and no one will put it out, \q because of the evil you have done.

L.4: Be circumcised to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and remove the foreskins of your heart, \q man of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, \q or {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will go out like fire, and burn, and there will be no one to quench [it], \q because of the evil of your deeds.

R.4: Circumcise yourselves to belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Circumcise your hearts: open them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q you people of Judah and Jerusalem. \q If you do not, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger will blaze out like a fire. It will burn, and no one will be able to put it out, \q because of the evil things you have done.

decisions.choice: remove the foreskins of your heart: the command of Deuteronomy 10:16
decisions.reason: Moses told Israel to "circumcise the foreskin of your heart" (Deuteronomy 10:16) and promised that the LORD would one day do it himself (Deuteronomy 30:6). Jeremiah repeats the command to a people who bear the sign in their bodies but not in their hearts (9:24-25).

decisions.choice: circumcise yourselves to the LORD: make the covenant sign true on the inside, belonging wholly to him
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of the covenant on the body (Genesis 17:10-14). An uncircumcised heart is closed and unwilling to hear (Leviticus 26:41; Jeremiah 6:10 uses the same picture for the ear). To circumcise oneself "to the LORD" is to remove what closes the heart to him and to give oneself to him.

decisions.choice: my wrath will go out like fire, with no one to quench it: a judgment that cannot be stopped once it starts
decisions.reason: The same words return in 21:12 and Amos 5:6. A fire that no one can put out is a judgment that runs its course; the call to repent comes before it starts.

decisions.choice: circumcise your hearts
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the wording of Deuteronomy 10:16, which leaves out "foreskins" because "circumcise your hearts" already carries the picture. Literal keeps the full wording. Readable adds what it means, "open them to me", as Deuteronomy 10:16 does.

decisions.choice: people of Judah and (people of) Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, the singular "man" and the word "inhabitants" mean everyone who lives there.

records.source: הַגִּ֣ידוּ בִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הַשְׁמִ֔יעוּ וְאִמְר֕וּ תִּקְע֥וּ שׁוֹפָ֖ר בָּאָ֑רֶץ קִרְא֤וּ מַלְאוּ֙ וְאִמְר֔וּ הֵאָסְפ֥וּ וְנָב֖וֹאָה אֶל־עָרֵ֥י הַמִּבְצָֽר׃
records.gloss: Declare in Judah, and in Jerusalem proclaim, and say: Blow [the] shofar in the land; call out, fill, and say: Gather yourselves and let us go into [the] cities of the fortification.
pieces: Announce it in Judah, proclaim it in Jerusalem, and say, \q "Blow the ram's horn throughout the land!" \q Shout at the top of your voice and say, \q "Gather together! Let us go into the fortified cities!"

L.5: Declare in Judah, and in Jerusalem proclaim, and say, \q "Blow the trumpet in the land!" \q Cry out, [with] full [voice], and say, \q "Gather together, and let us go into the fortified cities!"

R.5: Announce this in Judah and in Jerusalem. Tell them: \q "Blow the trumpet everywhere in the land!" \q Shout as loud as you can: \q "Come together! Let us run to the cities with strong walls!"

decisions.choice: the shofar blown in the land: the alarm for an enemy attack
decisions.reason: The shofar, a ram's horn, was blown to warn of an enemy and to call people to arms or to shelter (6:1; Hosea 5:8; Amos 3:6). Here it warns of the invader of verses 6-7.

decisions.choice: call out, fill: cry with a full voice
decisions.reason: The two verbs stand side by side with no object. "Fill" means fill the voice: shout loudly. The heralds are to cry the warning as loud as they can (12:6 has "they call after you fully").

decisions.choice: fortified cities: walled towns where people from the open country took refuge
decisions.reason: When an army invaded, people left their villages and fields for the walled towns (8:14; 35:11). The cry shows that the danger is close.

decisions.choice: the LORD sends heralds through the land; what they are to cry is quoted
decisions.reason: The commands are plural: heralds are told to spread the alarm. The words of the alarm itself, "Blow ..." and "Gather ...", are what they are to say.

decisions.choice: trumpet (L, R); ram's horn (B)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for the shofar, as in Isaiah: Literal and Readable say "trumpet", Balanced "ram's horn" (m1).

decisions.choice: cities with strong walls
decisions.reason: Readable says what made a city "fortified" (m3).

records.source: שְׂאוּ־נֵ֣ס צִיּ֔וֹנָה הָעִ֖יזוּ אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹ֑דוּ כִּ֣י רָעָ֗ה אָנֹכִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא מִצָּפ֖וֹן וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: Lift up a signal flag toward Zion; flee for safety, do not stand still, for evil I am bringing from [the] north, and great destruction.
pieces: Raise a signal flag toward Zion! \q Run for safety; do not wait! \q For I am bringing disaster from the north, a great and crushing ruin.

L.6: Lift up a signal flag toward Zion; \q flee for safety, do not stand still! \q For evil I am bringing from the north, and a great breaking.

R.6: Put up a signal flag that points the way to Zion! \q Run for safety! Do not wait! \q For I am bringing disaster from the north. It will crush everything.

decisions.choice: a signal flag toward Zion: a banner on a pole showing refugees the way to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: A signal flag was raised on a pole or a hilltop to call people together or show them where to go (Isaiah 5:26; 11:12). Here it points the people of the countryside to Zion, Jerusalem, as the place of refuge.

decisions.choice: evil: disaster, harm
decisions.reason: The word means what is bad, whether wrongdoing or the harm that comes on people. Here it is the disaster the LORD brings as judgment, not wrongdoing on his part (as in Isaiah 45:7; Jeremiah 1:14).

decisions.choice: from the north: the invader foretold in Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: In 1:13-15 disaster boils over "from the north". The enemy is not named in these chapters (6:1, 22); later it is named as Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar (20:4; 25:9). Armies from Mesopotamia came into Israel from the north, along the curve of fertile land.

decisions.choice: great destruction: a great breaking, a crash
decisions.reason: The word means breaking or fracture, as of a bone or a wall. It returns in verse 20 and through the book for the collapse of the nation (6:1; 8:21; 14:17).

decisions.choice: a great and crushing ruin / It will crush everything
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the picture of breaking in "destruction" (m4).

records.source: עָלָ֤ה אַרְיֵה֙ מִֽסֻּבְּכ֔וֹ וּמַשְׁחִ֣ית גּוֹיִ֔ם נָסַ֖ע יָצָ֣א מִמְּקֹמ֑וֹ לָשׂ֤וּם אַרְצֵךְ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה עָרַ֥יִךְ תִּצֶּ֖ינָה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃
records.gloss: Has gone up a lion from his thicket, and a destroyer of nations has set out; he has gone out from his place to make your land a waste; your cities will be laid in ruins, without inhabitant.
pieces: A lion has left his thicket; \q a destroyer of nations has broken camp. \q He has left his place \q to make your land a wasteland. \q Your towns will lie in ruins, with no one living in them.

L.7: A lion has come up from his thicket, \q and a destroyer of nations has set out; \q he has gone out from his place \q to make your land a waste; \q your cities will fall in ruins, without inhabitant.

R.7: A lion has come out of the bushes where it hides. \q One who destroys nations is on the march. \q He has left his home \q to turn your land into a wasteland. \q Your towns will be ruins, and no one will live in them.

decisions.choice: a lion ... a destroyer of nations: the invading king and his army
decisions.reason: The lion is a picture of the enemy from the north (verse 6), who leaves his lair to hunt (2:15; 5:6; 50:17, where the lion is named as the king of Babylon). "Destroyer of nations" says plainly what the lion is.

decisions.choice: set out: pulled up the tent pegs, broke camp
decisions.reason: The verb is used for breaking camp and moving on (Genesis 35:5; Numbers 10:12). The army is already on the move.

decisions.choice: a waste ... laid in ruins: the land made desolate, the towns emptied
decisions.reason: The first word means a place so ruined that people are appalled at it (2:15; 5:30). The second verb means to be laid waste, to fall in ruins; with "without inhabitant" it pictures towns left empty.

decisions.choice: the bushes where it hides
decisions.reason: Readable explains "thicket", the dense undergrowth where a lion lies hidden.

records.source: עַל־זֹ֛את חִגְר֥וּ שַׂקִּ֖ים סִפְד֣וּ וְהֵילִ֑ילוּ כִּ֥י לֹא־שָׁ֛ב חֲר֥וֹן אַף־יְהֹוָ֖ה מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃פ
records.gloss: Because of this put on sackcloth, lament and wail, for not has turned back [the] burning of [the] anger of Yahweh from us.
pieces: So dress in sackcloth, lament and wail, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s fierce anger has still not turned away from us.

L.8: Because of this, gird on sackcloth, lament and wail; \q for the burning anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has not turned back from us.

R.8: So put on rough clothes to show your sorrow. Mourn and cry out in grief! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is still burning with anger against us. It has not turned away from us.

decisions.choice: put on sackcloth: dress in mourning
decisions.reason: Sackcloth was rough cloth of goat hair, tied around the waist in times of grief, repentance or disaster (6:26; Genesis 37:34; Isaiah 22:12).

decisions.choice: the burning of the anger of the LORD: his fierce anger
decisions.reason: The word for anger also means "nose", from the flaring nostrils of an angry person; with "burning" it describes anger at its height (verse 26; 25:37; Exodus 32:12).

decisions.choice: us: the prophet speaks as one of the people
decisions.reason: The prophet calls the people to mourn and counts himself among those under God's anger, as he does again in verse 13.

decisions.choice: rough clothes to show your sorrow ... cry out in grief
decisions.reason: Readable explains what sackcloth was for (m1) and uses the book-wide Readable wording "cry out in grief" for "wail", as Isaiah does.

records.source: וְהָיָ֤ה בַיּוֹם־הַהוּא֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה יֹאבַ֥ד לֵב־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְלֵ֣ב הַשָּׂרִ֑ים וְנָשַׁ֨מּוּ֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וְהַנְּבִיאִ֖ים יִתְמָֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And it will be in the day that, declares Yahweh, will perish [the] heart of the king and [the] heart of the officials, and will be appalled the priests, and the prophets will be astounded.
pieces: On that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the king and the officials will lose heart; \q the priests will be horrified, \q and the prophets will be stunned.

L.9: And it will be in that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q [that] the heart of the king will fail, and the heart of the princes; \q and the priests will be appalled, \q and the prophets will be astounded.

R.9: At that time, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the king and his leaders will lose their courage. \q The priests will be shocked, \q and the prophets will be stunned.

decisions.choice: the heart will perish: courage will fail
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and courage. When it "perishes" a person loses nerve and cannot think what to do (Psalm 76:6 speaks of the stout-hearted stripped of strength).

decisions.choice: king, officials, priests, prophets: all who were meant to lead the nation
decisions.reason: Jeremiah names the same four groups as those who have led Judah astray (2:26; 8:1; 32:32). The prophets who promised peace (verse 10; 6:14) will be the most dumbfounded.

decisions.choice: princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for the king's chief men.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֞ר אֲהָ֣הּ׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אָכֵן֩ הַשֵּׁ֨א הִשֵּׁ֜אתָ לָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וְלִירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר שָׁל֖וֹם יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם וְנָגְעָ֥ה חֶ֖רֶב עַד־הַנָּֽפֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And I said, Alas, Lord Yahweh, surely deceiving you have deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, Peace will be to you; and has reached [the] sword to the throat.
pieces: Then I said, "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, truly {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have led this people and Jerusalem far astray with the words, \q 'You will have peace,' \q while the sword is pressing at their throats!"

L.10: Then I said, "Alas, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Surely {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have greatly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, \q 'You will have peace,' \q while the sword has reached to the throat!"

R.10: Then I said, "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! You have truly fooled these people and Jerusalem! They were told, \q 'You will have peace.' \q But now a sword is at their throats!"

decisions.choice: you have deceived this people: the prophet's grieving complaint that God let the false promise of peace stand
alternatives: God himself sent the message of peace
the people deceived themselves, and the prophet speaks loosely
decisions.reason: The verb means to lead astray with false hope (2 Kings 18:29; 19:10; Jeremiah 29:8). The prophets of Jeremiah's day kept promising "peace" (6:14; 14:13; 23:17), and Jeremiah, in anguish, speaks as if God were responsible, because God allowed their message to go unchecked. Elsewhere the LORD says plainly that he did not send them (14:14; 23:21). Scripture can speak of God giving those who refuse the truth over to a lying message (1 Kings 22:20-23; Ezekiel 14:9). The words are a cry of grief like the laments of 15:18 and 20:7, not a teaching that God lies (Numbers 23:19).

decisions.choice: and I said: the prophet speaks
alternatives: and they will say: the leaders of verse 9 speak these words
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "and I said", so the words are Jeremiah's. Some Greek manuscripts are reported to read "and they will say" or "and they said", which would make the complaint that of the stunned priests and prophets of verse 9. The Hebrew reading is kept.

decisions.choice: surely deceiving you have deceived: the verb doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated, which strengthens it: "you have utterly deceived". The opening word "surely" adds to the force of the complaint.

decisions.choice: the sword has reached to the throat: their very life is under threat
decisions.reason: The word for "throat" also means life or self. The people were promised peace while the enemy's sword was already at their necks.

decisions.choice: Alas (L); Oh (B, R) ... Lord GOD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has a cry of dismay followed by "my Lord" and the divine name, written "Lord GOD" (or "Lord Yahweh" by the reader's setting) so that "Lord" is not written twice, as in Joshua 7:7.

decisions.choice: They were told
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "saying" does not say who spoke the words of peace. Readable keeps that open with "They were told" rather than naming God or the prophets as the speaker.

records.source: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא יֵאָמֵ֤ר לָֽעָם־הַזֶּה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם ר֣וּחַ צַ֤ח שְׁפָיִים֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר דֶּ֖רֶךְ בַּת־עַמִּ֑י ל֥וֹא לִזְר֖וֹת וְל֥וֹא לְהָבַֽר׃
records.gloss: At the time that it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: A wind hot of [the] bare heights in the wilderness [is the] way of [the] daughter of my people, not to winnow and not to cleanse;
pieces: At that time this people and Jerusalem will be told: \q "A scorching wind off the bare hills in the desert \q is blowing toward {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dear people, \q not to winnow and not to clean the grain;

L.11: At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: \q "A scorching wind from the bare heights in the wilderness \q [comes] toward the daughter of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q not to winnow and not to cleanse;

R.11: At that time these people and Jerusalem will be told: \q "A burning hot wind is blowing from the bare hills in the desert \q toward {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q It is not the gentle wind that farmers use to separate the grain from the straw.

decisions.choice: a scorching wind from the bare heights in the wilderness: the hot east wind off the desert
decisions.reason: A dry, burning wind blows in from the eastern desert, withering plants and bringing dust (18:17; Hosea 13:15). The coming army will sweep over the land like it.

decisions.choice: not to winnow and not to cleanse: not the light breeze used to separate grain from chaff
decisions.reason: Farmers tossed threshed grain into the air on a breezy day; the wind carried off the chaff and the grain fell back clean (15:7; Ruth 3:2). This wind is far too strong for that (verse 12): it does not sift the people, it sweeps everything away.

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people: God's people spoken of with tenderness, as a daughter
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures the people as a beloved daughter, especially when they suffer (8:11, 19-23; 14:17; Lamentations 2:11). It is a term of affection and grief, not a separate group within the people.

decisions.choice: what will be said runs on to the end of verse 12, where the LORD speaks of himself
decisions.reason: The words of the announcement continue into verse 12, which speaks of the wind coming "for me" and ends with "I will speak judgments". The message announced to the people is the LORD's own.

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people (L); my dear people (B); my people (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for this phrase, decided here at its first use in Jeremiah. Literal keeps the Hebrew picture; Balanced keeps its tenderness in "my dear people"; Readable says simply "my people" (m3).

decisions.choice: to clean the grain / the gentle wind that farmers use to separate the grain from the straw
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what winnowing and cleansing are done to, and Readable explains the practice (m2).

records.source: ר֧וּחַ מָלֵ֛א מֵאֵ֖לֶּה יָ֣בוֹא לִ֑י עַתָּ֕ה גַּם־אֲנִ֛י אֲדַבֵּ֥ר מִשְׁפָּטִ֖ים אוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: a wind full from these comes for me; now also I will speak judgments [with] them.
pieces: a wind too strong for that comes at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} command. \q Now I, too, will pronounce judgment on them."

L.12: a wind too strong for these comes for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q Now I also will speak judgments against them."

R.12: The wind I send is much too strong for that. \q Now I will announce {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sentence against them."

decisions.choice: too full for these: too strong for winnowing and cleansing
decisions.reason: "Full" here means strong, at full force. "These" points back to the winnowing and cleansing of verse 11: the wind is too violent for such work.

decisions.choice: for me: at my bidding, in my service
decisions.reason: The wind comes "for me", that is, on the LORD's errand. The enemy army is his instrument of judgment, as Babylon is called his servant in 25:9.

decisions.choice: speak judgments with them: pass sentence on them, as a judge does in court
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in 1:16 for the LORD's sentence on his people, and in 39:5 for the king of Babylon passing sentence on Zedekiah. "I also" sets the LORD's verdict against what the people have done.

decisions.choice: at my command / The wind I send
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "for me" means (m2).

records.source: הִנֵּ֣ה׀כַּעֲנָנִ֣ים יַעֲלֶ֗ה וְכַסּוּפָה֙ מַרְכְּבוֹתָ֔יו קַלּ֥וּ מִנְּשָׁרִ֖ים סוּסָ֑יו א֥וֹי לָ֖נוּ כִּ֥י שֻׁדָּֽדְנוּ׃
records.gloss: Look, like clouds he comes up, and like the storm wind his chariots; swifter than eagles his horses. Woe to us, for we are devastated!
pieces: See, he rises like gathering clouds, his chariots like a storm wind; \q his horses are quicker than eagles. \q "Woe to us! We are ruined!"

L.13: Look, like clouds he comes up, and like the storm wind [are] his chariots; \q his horses are swifter than eagles. \q "Woe to us, for we are devastated!"

R.13: Look! The enemy is coming like storm clouds. His chariots race like a whirlwind. \q His horses are faster than eagles. \q "How terrible this is for us! We are ruined!"

decisions.choice: he: the invader, the lion and destroyer of verse 7
decisions.reason: No subject is named. The verb is singular and the chariots and horses are "his", so the one coming is the enemy king with his army (verse 7).

decisions.choice: eagles: large birds of prey, eagles or vultures
decisions.reason: The word covers the great birds of prey. It is used for the speed of an attacking nation in Deuteronomy 28:49 and Habakkuk 1:8.

decisions.choice: woe to us: the people's cry breaks in
decisions.reason: The voice changes: the people, seeing the army coming, cry out. Their words are set apart as a quotation.

decisions.choice: The enemy ... How terrible this is for us
decisions.reason: Readable names "the enemy" as the one who comes (m1), and uses the book-wide Readable wording for a cry of "woe" said of oneself.

records.source: כַּבְּסִ֨י מֵרָעָ֤ה לִבֵּךְ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לְמַ֖עַן תִּוָּשֵׁ֑עִי עַד־מָתַ֛י תָּלִ֥ין בְּקִרְבֵּ֖ךְ מַחְשְׁב֥וֹת אוֹנֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Wash from evil your heart, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. Until when will lodge within you thoughts of your wickedness?
pieces: Jerusalem, wash the evil from your heart, \q so that you may be saved. \q How long will you let your wicked schemes make their home in you?

L.14: Wash your heart from evil, Jerusalem, \q so that you may be saved. \q How long will the thoughts of your wickedness lodge within you?

R.14: Jerusalem, wash the evil out of your heart, \q so that you can be saved. \q How long will you keep thinking evil thoughts?

decisions.choice: wash your heart from evil: be cleansed within
decisions.reason: The verb is used for washing clothes. Here it is the inner person that must be scrubbed clean (2:22; Isaiah 1:16; Psalm 51:4, 9). Even now, with the enemy coming, there is still a way to be saved.

decisions.choice: lodge: stay the night, settle in as a guest
decisions.reason: The verb means to spend the night. Wicked thoughts are pictured as guests who have moved in and will not leave.

decisions.choice: thoughts of your wickedness: plans for doing wrong
decisions.reason: The first word means plans or schemes; the second means trouble or wickedness, harm done to others. The same word means "disaster" in verse 15: the evil they plan brings evil on them.

decisions.choice: make their home in you
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of guests settling in (m2) in a natural phrase.

records.source: כִּ֛י ק֥וֹל מַגִּ֖יד מִדָּ֑ן וּמַשְׁמִ֥יעַ אָ֖וֶן מֵהַ֥ר אֶפְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: For a voice declaring from Dan, and proclaiming trouble from [the] hill country of Ephraim.
pieces: For a voice is announcing from Dan, \q proclaiming disaster from the hill country of Ephraim.

L.15: For a voice is declaring from Dan, \q and proclaiming trouble from the hill country of Ephraim.

R.15: Listen! A messenger is bringing news from Dan in the far north. \q Someone from the hills of Ephraim is announcing that disaster is coming.

decisions.choice: from Dan ... from the hill country of Ephraim: the news coming nearer and nearer
decisions.reason: Dan was the northernmost town of Israel ("from Dan to Beersheba", Judges 20:1). The hill country of Ephraim lies just north of Jerusalem and Benjamin. The report of the invader is passed south from town to town, each time closer.

decisions.choice: a voice: a messenger's shout, or simply "Listen!"
decisions.reason: The word means voice or sound and is often used as a call to attention, "Hark!" (3:21; 10:22). Here it is the shout of the one who brings the news.

decisions.choice: trouble: disaster
decisions.reason: The same word as "wickedness" in verse 14. Here it means the harm that is coming on them.

decisions.choice: Listen! A messenger ... in the far north
decisions.reason: Readable takes "a voice" as a call to attention and a messenger (m2), and says where Dan was (m1).

records.source: הַזְכִּ֣ירוּ לַגּוֹיִ֗ם הִנֵּה֙ הַשְׁמִ֣יעוּ עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם נֹצְרִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים מֵאֶ֣רֶץ הַמֶּרְחָ֑ק וַֽיִּתְּנ֛וּ עַל־עָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה קוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: Make [it] known to the nations, look, proclaim against Jerusalem: Besiegers are coming from [the] land of the distance, and they have given against [the] cities of Judah their voice.
pieces: Report to the nations: look! Announce it against Jerusalem: \q "Besiegers are coming from a far country; \q they shout their war cry against the towns of Judah."

L.16: Make [it] known to the nations, look! Proclaim against Jerusalem: \q "Besiegers are coming from a distant land, \q and they raise their voice against the cities of Judah."

R.16: Warn the nations! Listen! Tell Jerusalem what is coming: \q "Enemies are coming from a land far away to surround the city. \q They are shouting their battle cries against the towns of Judah."

decisions.choice: make it known: report, bring to notice
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause someone to remember or take note. The nations are to hear what is about to happen to Jerusalem, as witnesses to the LORD's judgment (6:18).

decisions.choice: besiegers: watchers, those who keep guard around a city
decisions.reason: The word means watchers or guards. Here it is the enemy who will surround the city and watch it so that no one gets in or out. Verse 17 plays on it: they are like watchmen around a field.

decisions.choice: they have given their voice: they raise the battle shout
decisions.reason: To "give voice" against a city is to shout the war cry before an attack (2:15, of lions roaring; 25:30).

decisions.choice: Enemies ... to surround the city
decisions.reason: Readable explains "besiegers" (m2).

records.source: כְּשֹׁמְרֵ֣י שָׂדַ֔י הָי֥וּ עָלֶ֖יהָ מִסָּבִ֑יב כִּי־אֹתִ֥י מָרָ֖תָה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Like keepers of a field they are against her all around, for me she has rebelled against, declares Yahweh.
pieces: Like watchmen guarding a field they surround her, \q because she has rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.17: Like guards of a field they are against her round about, \q for she has rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.17: They surround Jerusalem like guards around a field, \q because she has turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: keepers of a field: watchmen posted around a field of crops
decisions.reason: Farmers set watchmen on every side of a field near harvest, to keep thieves and animals out (compare Isaiah 1:8). The besiegers will ring Jerusalem as closely, so that nothing passes.

decisions.choice: her ... she: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The pronouns are feminine and refer to Jerusalem, named in verse 16 and pictured as a woman, as again in verses 30-31.

decisions.choice: rebelled: defied, been bitterly disobedient
decisions.reason: The verb is used of defiance against God's word and command (5:23; Deuteronomy 1:26; 9:23).

decisions.choice: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names the city instead of "her" (m2).

records.source: דַּרְכֵּךְ֙ וּמַ֣עֲלָלַ֔יִךְ עָשׂ֥וֹ אֵ֖לֶּה לָ֑ךְ זֹ֤את רָעָתֵךְ֙ כִּ֣י מָ֔ר כִּ֥י נָגַ֖ע עַד־לִבֵּֽךְ׃ס
records.gloss: Your way and your deeds have done these to you; this [is] your evil, for [it is] bitter, for it has reached to your heart.
pieces: Your conduct and your deeds \q have brought this on you. \q This is what your evil brings: how bitter it is, \q how it pierces to your heart!

L.18: Your way and your deeds \q have done these things to you. \q This [is] your evil; how bitter [it is]! \q How it has reached to your heart!

R.18: The way you have lived and the things you have done \q have brought this on you. \q This disaster is what your evil has brought. It is bitter! \q It hurts you deep in your heart.

decisions.choice: your evil: your wickedness and the disaster it brings, both at once
decisions.reason: The word means both wrongdoing and calamity (verse 6). Here the two meet: the disaster is their own wickedness coming back on them, as 2:19 says, "your evil will discipline you".

decisions.choice: for ... for: "how" in an exclamation
decisions.reason: The small word usually means "for" or "that", but here it introduces two exclamations: how bitter it is, how it reaches the heart.

decisions.choice: it has reached to your heart: it strikes to the very center of you
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in verse 10 of the sword reaching the throat. Here the bitterness pierces to the heart, the center of life and thought.

decisions.choice: what your evil brings / This disaster is what your evil has brought
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bare "your evil". Balanced and Readable spell out both sides of the word (m1): the disaster that their wrongdoing brought.

records.source: מֵעַ֣י׀מֵעַ֨י׀אוֹחִ֜ילָה קִיר֥וֹת לִבִּ֛י הֹֽמֶה־לִּ֥י לִבִּ֖י לֹ֣א אַחֲרִ֑ישׁ כִּ֣י ק֤וֹל שׁוֹפָר֙ שָׁמַ֣עַתְּ נַפְשִׁ֔י תְּרוּעַ֖ת מִלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: My inward parts, my inward parts! I writhe! [The] walls of my heart! Is pounding to me my heart; not I can keep silent, for [the] sound of [the] shofar you have heard, my soul, [the] shout of war.
pieces: My insides, my insides! I twist in pain! My chest is bursting! My heart pounds within me; I cannot keep quiet, \q for you have heard it, my soul: the sound of the ram's horn, \q the battle cry of war.

L.19: My bowels, my bowels! I writhe in pain! The walls of my heart! My heart is pounding within me; I cannot keep silent, \q for you have heard, my soul, the sound of the trumpet, \q the battle cry of war.

R.19: Oh, the pain deep inside me! I am twisting in pain! My heart is pounding hard inside me. I cannot keep quiet, \q because I have heard the trumpet blowing. \q It is the alarm call for war.

decisions.choice: my inward parts: the depths of my feelings
decisions.reason: The word means the bowels or inner organs, the place where deep emotion is felt (Isaiah 16:11; Lamentations 1:20; Song of Songs 5:4). The cry is one of deep, physical anguish.

decisions.choice: the speaker: the prophet, crying out in anguish at what he sees coming
decisions.reason: Verses 19-21 are spoken by one person. It is most likely Jeremiah himself, overwhelmed by the vision of the invasion (8:18-23; 9:9). Because he speaks of "my tents" in verse 20, he also gives voice to the land and its people, whose ruin he shares. The LORD's answer comes in verse 22.

decisions.choice: I writhe ... you have heard, my soul: the forms read aloud in the tradition
alternatives: I wait ... I have heard, my soul
decisions.reason: In two places the Hebrew text has one form written and another marked to be read. In the first, both forms are usually taken as "I writhe"; the written one can also be read from a verb meaning "wait" or "hope". In the second, the written form is "I have heard", the form to be read is "you have heard, my soul". The sense is the same either way: the prophet himself has heard the alarm.

decisions.choice: the walls of my heart ... my heart is pounding: the heart hammering inside the chest
decisions.reason: The "walls" of the heart are the chest around it, or the heart itself pictured as a house. The verb is used of the roar of the sea and of a crowd: the heart is in turmoil.

decisions.choice: the sound of the shofar, the shout of war: the signals of battle
decisions.reason: The shofar sounded the alarm (verse 5), and the war cry was the shout raised as battle began (49:2; Amos 1:14).

decisions.choice: My insides ... My chest is bursting (B); the pain deep inside me (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "bowels" and "the walls of my heart", the Hebrew pictures. Balanced says "insides" and "my chest", the wall around the heart (m4), and Readable says what the cry means (m1).

decisions.choice: I have heard
decisions.reason: The prophet addresses his own soul, "you have heard, my soul", meaning "I myself have heard" (m3). Readable says "I have heard".

records.heading: Anguish at the sound of war

records.source: שֶׁ֤בֶר עַל־שֶׁ֨בֶר֙ נִקְרָ֔א כִּ֥י שֻׁדְּדָ֖ה כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ פִּתְאֹם֙ שֻׁדְּד֣וּ אֹהָלַ֔י רֶ֖גַע יְרִיעֹתָֽי׃
records.gloss: Destruction upon destruction is proclaimed, for is devastated all the land; suddenly are devastated my tents, [in] a moment my curtains.
pieces: Word comes of ruin upon ruin; \q the whole land lies devastated. \q Without warning my tents are torn down, \q my curtains in an instant.

L.20: Destruction upon destruction is proclaimed, \q for the whole land is devastated; \q suddenly my tents are devastated, \q in a moment my curtains.

R.20: News comes of one disaster after another. \q The whole country is destroyed. \q Suddenly my tents are destroyed. \q In a moment the curtains of my home are torn down.

decisions.choice: destruction upon destruction is proclaimed: one report of disaster follows another
decisions.reason: The word is the "great destruction" of verse 6, a breaking or crash. "Is proclaimed" means it is announced, or cried out: news of each new collapse comes in after the last.

decisions.choice: my tents ... my curtains: my home
decisions.reason: Tents and their curtains were an old way of speaking of one's home, even for people living in houses (10:20; 2 Samuel 20:1). The speaker's own household is struck as the land falls (m2 at verse 19).

decisions.choice: News comes of
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take "is proclaimed" as the arrival of reports (m1).

decisions.choice: the curtains of my home
decisions.reason: Readable adds "of my home" to show what the tents stand for (m2).

records.source: עַד־מָתַ֖י אֶרְאֶה־נֵּ֑ס אֶשְׁמְעָ֖ה ק֥וֹל שׁוֹפָֽר׃ס
records.gloss: Until when will I see a signal flag, will I hear [the] sound of [the] shofar?
pieces: How long must I look at the signal flag \q and listen to the ram's horn?

L.21: How long must I see the signal flag, \q [and] hear the sound of the trumpet?

R.21: How long must I see the signal flags of war \q and hear the trumpet calling to battle?

decisions.choice: the signal flag and the shofar: the signs of war going on
decisions.reason: The same flag and horn that called the people to flee (verses 5-6) now mark a war that seems never to end. The question "how long" is a lament (12:4; Psalm 13:2).

decisions.choice: of war ... calling to battle
decisions.reason: Readable says what the flag and the trumpet signal (m1).

records.source: כִּ֣י׀אֱוִ֣יל עַמִּ֗י אוֹתִי֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ בָּנִ֤ים סְכָלִים֙ הֵ֔מָּה וְלֹ֥א נְבוֹנִ֖ים הֵ֑מָּה חֲכָמִ֥ים הֵ֨מָּה֙ לְהָרַ֔ע וּלְהֵיטִ֖יב לֹ֥א יָדָֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: For foolish [is] my people; me they do not know; children stupid [are] they, and not understanding [are] they; wise [are] they to do evil, but to do good they do not know.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people are fools; they do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q They are senseless children; \q they have no understanding. \q They are skilled at doing evil, \q but they do not know how to do good.

L.22: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people are foolish; {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they do not know; \q they are stupid children, \q and they have no understanding. \q They are wise at doing evil, \q but to do good they do not know [how].

R.22: This is happening because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people are foolish. They do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q They are like silly children \q who understand nothing. \q They are experts at doing wrong, \q but they do not know how to do what is right.

decisions.choice: my people ... me: the LORD answers the prophet's lament
decisions.reason: The speaker changes from the prophet (verses 19-21) to the LORD, who gives the reason for the disaster. The word "for" ties his answer to the cry "how long".

decisions.choice: know: acknowledge, be in a close relationship with
decisions.reason: To know the LORD is more than knowing facts about him: it is to trust and obey him and live in his covenant (2:8; 9:23; 22:16; Hosea 4:1).

decisions.choice: foolish, stupid, without understanding: moral folly, not lack of intelligence
decisions.reason: The words describe people who have the wit to plan evil well but refuse to live wisely before God (Proverbs 1:7). They are clever in the wrong things.

decisions.choice: This is happening because
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "for" points back to: the disaster of verses 19-21 (m1).

records.source: רָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהִנֵּה־תֹ֖הוּ וָבֹ֑הוּ וְאֶל־הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֵ֥ין אוֹרָֽם׃
records.gloss: I looked at the earth, and look, formlessness and emptiness; and to the heavens, and there was not their light.
pieces: I looked at the earth, and it was without form and empty; \q I looked to the heavens, and their light was gone.

L.23: I looked at the earth, and look, [it was] formlessness and emptiness; \q and to the heavens, and their light [was] not [there].

R.23: I looked at the earth. It did not have any shape, and it was empty. \q I looked up at the sky, and there was no light.

decisions.choice: formless and empty, with no light: the world as it was before God's first word in Genesis 1:2-3
decisions.reason: The rhyming pair of words appears together only here and in Genesis 1:2 (Isaiah 34:11 sets them in parallel lines). In Genesis the earth was formless and empty and dark until God said, "Let there be light". In Jeremiah's vision the judgment runs creation backward: the land returns to that state, and the light is gone.

decisions.choice: I looked ... and look: a vision, told in four matching lines
decisions.reason: Verses 23-26 each begin "I looked, and look". The prophet describes what he saw in a vision of the coming judgment; the repeated words give it the shape of a poem in four stanzas.

decisions.choice: the earth: the whole earth in the vision
decisions.reason: The word can mean the land or the whole earth. Set beside "the heavens" and the words of Genesis 1:2, it is the earth in this vision, although the judgment it pictures falls on Judah (verses 26-27).

decisions.choice: formlessness and emptiness (L); without form and empty (B); did not have any shape ... empty (R)
decisions.reason: Each level uses its own wording from Genesis 1:2, so that a reader of either passage hears the other (m1).

decisions.choice: (look left out) ... I looked to the heavens / I looked up at the sky
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out the second "look", which Literal keeps, and repeat "I looked" where the Hebrew lets it be understood.

records.source: רָאִ֨יתִי֙ הֶֽהָרִ֔ים וְהִנֵּ֖ה רֹעֲשִׁ֑ים וְכָל־הַגְּבָע֖וֹת הִתְקַלְקָֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: I looked at the mountains, and look, quaking; and all the hills shook to and fro.
pieces: I looked at the mountains, and they were quaking; \q all the hills were rocking back and forth.

L.24: I looked at the mountains, and look, [they were] quaking, \q and all the hills were swaying.

R.24: I looked at the mountains, and they were shaking. \q All the hills were swaying back and forth.

decisions.choice: the mountains quaking: even what is most firm gives way
decisions.reason: Mountains stand for what is solid and lasting (Psalm 46:3-4; Isaiah 54:10). When the LORD comes in judgment they shake (Nahum 1:5; Judges 5:5).

decisions.choice: shook to and fro: swayed lightly back and forth
decisions.reason: The verb comes from a root meaning "light". The hills rock as if they had no weight.

decisions.choice: (look left out)
decisions.reason: As in verse 23, Balanced and Readable leave out "look", which Literal keeps.

records.source: רָאִ֕יתִי וְהִנֵּ֖ה אֵ֣ין הָאָדָ֑ם וְכָל־ע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נָדָֽדוּ׃
records.gloss: I looked, and look, there was not the human, and all [the] birds of the heavens had fled.
pieces: I looked, and there was no one at all; \q every bird in the sky had flown away.

L.25: I looked, and look, there was no human being, \q and all the birds of the heavens had fled.

R.25: I looked, and there were no people. \q All the birds had flown away.

decisions.choice: no human, no birds: the creatures of the fifth and sixth days gone
decisions.reason: In Genesis 1 the birds were made on the fifth day and humankind on the sixth (Genesis 1:20, 26-27). The vision takes them away again (compare 9:9; Zephaniah 1:3; Hosea 4:3).

decisions.choice: the human: humankind, people
decisions.reason: The word with the article means humankind as a whole, men and women alike, not one man.

decisions.choice: (look left out)
decisions.reason: As in verse 23.

records.source: רָאִ֕יתִי וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַכַּרְמֶ֖ל הַמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְכָל־עָרָ֗יו נִתְּצוּ֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י חֲר֥וֹן אַפּֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: I looked, and look, the orchard land [was] the wilderness, and all its cities were pulled down before Yahweh, before [the] burning of his anger.
pieces: I looked, and the orchard land had become a desert; \q all its towns had been torn down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fierce anger.

L.26: I looked, and look, the orchard land [was] the wilderness, \q and all its cities were pulled down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} burning anger.

R.26: I looked, and the land of rich orchards had become a desert. \q All its towns had been torn down. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had done this in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fierce anger.

decisions.choice: the orchard land: the fertile, cultivated land
decisions.reason: The word means garden land, land planted with vines and fruit trees. In 2:7 the LORD brought Israel "into a land of orchards". It is not Mount Carmel here, since it is set against the desert as fruitful land against barren.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: the fruitful land has become the desert itself
decisions.reason: The two nouns stand side by side with no verb: the garden land "was the wilderness". It is the reverse of the promise that the desert would become a garden (Isaiah 32:15; 35:1-2).

decisions.choice: before the LORD, before his burning anger: at his presence, by his anger
decisions.reason: "Before" (literally "from the face of") means "because of, at the coming of". The ruin is the LORD's work, the fierce anger named in verse 8.

decisions.choice: the orchard land (L, B); the land of rich orchards (R)
decisions.reason: The word is "orchard" at every level, as in Isaiah. Here it names the whole fertile land (m1), so all three levels say "land".

decisions.choice: The LORD had done this
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "before the LORD" means (m3).

records.source: כִּי־כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שְׁמָמָ֥ה תִהְיֶ֖ה כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְכָלָ֖ה לֹ֥א אֶעֱשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh: A desolation will be all the land, but a full end not I will make.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q The whole land will be laid waste, \q but I will not destroy it completely.

L.27: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q A desolation the whole land will be, \q yet a full end I will not make.

R.27: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q The whole land will be ruined, \q but I will not destroy it completely.

decisions.choice: a full end: complete destruction, an end with nothing left
decisions.reason: The word means a finishing off, destruction to the last. The same promise, that the LORD will not make a full end, returns in 5:10, 18; 30:11 and 46:28: judgment will be severe, but a remnant will be left.

decisions.choice: but ... not: a limit set within the judgment
alternatives: and I will make a full end of it (a change of one letter)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "not". It has been suggested that the word be read with a different letter as "of it", which would make the line a threat of total destruction. The text as it stands is kept, and the same promise in 5:10 and 5:18 supports it.

decisions.choice: the land: the land of Judah
decisions.reason: The same word as "the earth" in verses 23 and 28. Here, with the cities of verse 26, it is the land that will be laid waste.

decisions.choice: destroy it completely
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "make a full end" as a plain verb.

records.source: עַל־זֹאת֙ תֶּאֱבַ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ וְקָדְר֥וּ הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם מִמָּ֑עַל עַ֤ל כִּי־דִבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ זַמֹּ֔תִי וְלֹ֥א נִחַ֖מְתִּי וְלֹא־אָשׁ֥וּב מִמֶּֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: Because of this will mourn the earth, and will grow dark the heavens above, because I have spoken, I have purposed, and not I have relented, and not I will turn back from it.
pieces: For this the earth will mourn, \q and the sky above will turn dark, \q because I have spoken and I have decided; \q I have not changed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mind, and I will not turn back from it.

L.28: On account of this the earth will mourn, \q and the heavens above will grow dark, \q because I have spoken, I have resolved, \q and I have not relented, and I will not turn back from it.

R.28: Because of this, the earth will mourn, \q and the sky will grow dark. \q I have spoken, and I have made up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mind. \q I will not change it, and I will not turn back.

decisions.choice: the earth will mourn, the heavens grow dark: all creation grieves at the judgment
decisions.reason: The earth is pictured as a mourner and the sky as putting on dark clothes of grief (12:4; Isaiah 50:3; Hosea 4:3; Joel 2:10). The word "earth" here, as in verse 23, is wider than the land of verse 27.

decisions.choice: purposed: planned, resolved
decisions.reason: The verb means to form a plan and hold to it (51:12; Lamentations 2:17).

decisions.choice: I have not relented: I have not changed my course
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the LORD turning from a judgment he had announced when people repent (18:8; 26:3, 13, 19; Jonah 3:10). Here, with Judah unrepentant, he will not turn back.

decisions.choice: changed my mind / I will not change it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "relent" in everyday words.

records.source: מִקּ֨וֹל פָּרָ֜שׁ וְרֹ֣מֵה קֶ֗שֶׁת בֹּרַ֨חַת֙ כָּל־הָעִ֔יר בָּ֚אוּ בֶּעָבִ֔ים וּבַכֵּפִ֖ים עָל֑וּ כָּל־הָעִ֣יר עֲזוּבָ֔ה וְאֵין־יוֹשֵׁ֥ב בָּהֵ֖ן אִֽישׁ׃
records.gloss: From [the] sound of horseman and shooter of bow fleeing [is] every the city; they go into thickets and among rocks they climb up; every the city [is] forsaken, and there is not dwelling in them a man.
pieces: At the sound of horsemen and archers \q the people of every town run away. \q They go into the thickets; they climb up among the rocks. \q Every town is abandoned; \q no one lives in them.

L.29: At the sound of horseman and bowman \q every city is fleeing; \q they go into the thickets, and among the rocks they climb; \q every city is forsaken, \q and no one lives in them.

R.29: When they hear the horsemen and the archers coming, \q the people in every town run away. \q They hide in the bushes and climb up among the rocks. \q All the towns are left empty. \q No one lives in them anymore.

decisions.choice: every the city: every city, the people of each town
decisions.reason: The words can mean "the whole city", but "in them" at the end of the verse shows that many towns are meant. The town stands for its people, who flee.

decisions.choice: thickets ... rocks: dense brush and rocky crags, places to hide
decisions.reason: The first word is rare and seems to mean thick undergrowth; the second means rocks or cliffs. In times of invasion people hid in caves, thickets and rocks (1 Samuel 13:6; Isaiah 2:19, 21).

decisions.choice: horseman and archer: the enemy's cavalry and bowmen
decisions.reason: The armies of Mesopotamia fought with horsemen, chariots and archers (6:23; 50:42). The words are singular, standing for the whole force.

decisions.choice: the people of every town
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the people" of each town flee (m1).

records.source: וְאַ֨תְּ שָׁד֜וּד מַֽה־תַּעֲשִׂ֗י כִּֽי־תִלְבְּשִׁ֨י שָׁנִ֜י כִּי־תַעְדִּ֣י עֲדִי־זָהָ֗ב כִּֽי־תִקְרְעִ֤י בַפּוּךְ֙ עֵינַ֔יִךְ לַשָּׁ֖וְא תִּתְיַפִּ֑י מָאֲסוּ־בָ֥ךְ עֹגְבִ֖ים נַפְשֵׁ֥ךְ יְבַקֵּֽשׁוּ׃
records.gloss: And you, devastated [one], what will you do? That you dress [in] scarlet, that you adorn [yourself with] ornaments of gold, that you enlarge with eye paint your eyes, in vain you make yourself beautiful; reject you lovers; your life they seek.
pieces: And you, ruined one, what will you do? Though you dress in scarlet, though you put on jewelry of gold, though you make your eyes look large with paint, \q you make yourself beautiful for nothing. \q Your lovers reject you; they are out to take your life.

L.30: And you, devastated one, what will you do? Though you dress in scarlet, though you adorn [yourself with] ornaments of gold, though you enlarge your eyes with paint, \q in vain you make yourself beautiful. \q [Your] lovers reject you; they seek your life.

R.30: And you, Jerusalem, now ruined, what will you do? You may dress in bright red clothes and wear gold jewelry. You may paint around your eyes to make them look bigger. \q But it is no use making yourself beautiful. \q The nations you tried to win as lovers hate you now. They want to kill you.

decisions.choice: you, devastated one: Jerusalem, spoken to as a woman
decisions.reason: The words are feminine singular, addressed to the city, which is named "the daughter of Zion" in verse 31. She is spoken of as already ruined, so sure is the judgment.

decisions.choice: scarlet, gold ornaments, eye paint: a woman dressing to attract
decisions.reason: Rich red cloth, gold jewelry and dark paint around the eyes were signs of wealth and beauty. Jezebel painted her eyes before she met Jehu (2 Kings 9:30), and Ezekiel 23:40 uses the same picture for Jerusalem courting other nations.

decisions.choice: lovers: the foreign nations Judah courted as allies
decisions.reason: Jeremiah pictures Judah's search for help from Egypt and Assyria as a woman chasing lovers (2:33, 36; 3:1; 22:20; 30:14). Those she courted will turn on her.

decisions.choice: they seek your life: they want to kill you
decisions.reason: To "seek someone's life" means to try to kill them (11:21; 19:7; Exodus 4:19).

decisions.choice: that ... that ... that: even though you do these things
decisions.reason: The three clauses with the small word usually meaning "that" or "for" set out what she does, and the line "in vain you make yourself beautiful" answers them all: none of it will help.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem ... The nations you tried to win as lovers
decisions.reason: Readable names the city (m1) and explains who the lovers are (m3).

records.source: כִּי֩ ק֨וֹל כְּחוֹלָ֜ה שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי צָרָה֙ כְּמַבְכִּירָ֔ה ק֧וֹל בַּת־צִיּ֛וֹן תִּתְיַפֵּ֖חַ תְּפָרֵ֣שׂ כַּפֶּ֑יהָ אֽוֹי־נָ֣א לִ֔י כִּֽי־עָיְפָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י לְהֹרְגִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: For a voice like [one] in labor I have heard, distress like [one] bearing a first child, [the] voice of [the] daughter of Zion; she gasps for breath, she spreads out her palms: Woe now to me, for faints my soul before killers!
pieces: I hear a scream like that of a woman in labor, the agony of one bearing her first child: \q it is the voice of Daughter Zion, fighting for breath and holding out her hands: \q "Woe is me! \q My life is ebbing away before killers!"

L.31: For a cry as of [a woman] in labor I have heard, distress as of [one] bearing her first child, \q the cry of the daughter of Zion; she gasps for breath, she spreads out her hands: \q "Woe [is] me now, \q for my soul faints before killers!"

R.31: I hear a cry like a woman giving birth, the painful cry of a woman having her first baby. \q It is the cry of the people of Zion, like a woman gasping for breath and reaching out her hands for help: \q "How terrible this is for me! \q I am fainting, and murderers are all around me!"

decisions.choice: like a woman in labor with her first child: helpless, overwhelming anguish
decisions.reason: The pain of childbirth is the prophets' picture for terror that cannot be escaped (6:24; 13:21; 22:23; 30:6; Isaiah 13:8). A first birth was known to be the hardest and most frightening.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Zion: Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a young woman
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah 1:8, Zion stands for Jerusalem, and "daughter" pictures the city and its people as a woman, loved and vulnerable. Here the picture is of a woman in labor who finds herself among killers.

decisions.choice: she spreads out her palms: a gesture of pleading for help
decisions.reason: Spreading out the hands was a gesture of prayer or of begging for help (Lamentations 1:17; Isaiah 1:15). Here no help comes.

decisions.choice: my soul faints before killers: my life is ebbing away in front of those who will kill me
decisions.reason: "Soul" means the self or life, and the verb means to be weary or faint. The murderers stand over her as she gives birth.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Zion (L); Daughter Zion (B); the people of Zion (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording, as in Isaiah. Readable says "the people of Zion" and keeps the picture of one woman with "like a woman", so that "her hands" and "me" still fit (m2).

decisions.choice: Woe is me (L, B); How terrible this is for me (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for a cry of woe said of oneself, as in Isaiah. Literal also keeps the small word "now", which strengthens the cry.

decisions.choice: for help ... are all around me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the outstretched hands mean (m3) and where the killers are (m4).
